chunks: And among what was narrated by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from one who informed him, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who cut off the head of a dead man. He said: «The indemnity is upon him, for indeed his sanctity in death is like his sanctity while he is alive.»

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial indemnity legally due for the violation
key_terms.حَيٌّ: alive; referring to the person’s state before death
key_terms.حُرْمَتَهُ: his inviolability and sanctity protected by the law
key_terms.رَأْسَ: the head of the deceased person that was severed
key_terms.مَيِّتٍ: a dead person; the one whose body was violated after death

ai.seo_question: Is there diyah for cutting off the head of a dead person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a legal ruling that cutting off the head of a deceased person entails liability for diyah. It affirms that the inviolability and sanctity of the human being remain after death, just as they were during life.
